**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

We run mariadb 10.1 and 10.2 in CI here as well as it being Red Hat's standard MySQL used in Openstack (which is where I work) and there is no issue.   We detect "mariadb" by looking for the string "MariaDB" in server version info.   So please let me know exactly:

1. version of MariaDB in use

2. linux (or other) distro in use, or otherwise what your source for MariaDB is

3. exact output of:  


```
#!

MariaDB [(none)]> select @@version;
+-----------------+
| @@version       |
+-----------------+
| 10.2.12-MariaDB |
+-----------------+
1 row in set (0.00 sec)



```

**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

note compat here is from #4120

**Curtis McCully ([@cmccully](https://github.com/cmccully)) wrote:**

**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

I've googled "maxscale" and this is a proxy server.   So that is likely getting in the way and subverting the version information sent over the wire within the protocol.   Can you run the equivalent of this script please:


```
>>> import pymysql
>>> conn = pymysql.connect(user='root', password='932134b56234b159a80e75c4c5d0b79b3e99155c', host="<your proxy server>")
>>> conn.server_version
u'5.5.5-10.1.20-MariaDB'

```

**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

also it looks like you're supposed to configure this:

https://mariadb.com/kb/en/mariadb-enterprise/maxscale-mariadb-version-mismatch/

https://mariadb.com/kb/en/mariadb-enterprise/mariadb-maxscale-21-mariadb-maxscale-configuration-usage-scenarios/#version_string

> version_string

> This parameter sets a custom version string that is sent in the MySQL Handshake from MariaDB MaxScale to clients.
> If not set, the default value is 5.5.5-10.0.0 MaxScale <MaxScale version> where <MaxScale version> is the version of MaxScale. If the provided string does not start with the number 5, a 5.5.5- prefix will be added to it. This means that a version_string value of MaxScale-Service would result in a 5.5.5-MaxScale-Service being sent to the client.

I can add a documentation note here but that is your issue.

**Curtis McCully ([@cmccully](https://github.com/cmccully)) wrote:**

Ah. Interesting. Thanks.

[GCC 4.4.7 20120313 (Red Hat 4.4.7-1)] on linux
Type "help", "copyright", "credits" or "license" for more information.
import pymysql
conn = pymysql.connect(user='****', password='****', host='host')
conn.server_version
'5.5.5-10.0.0 2.1.9-maxscale'

**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

even if I looked for "maxscale", that doesn't tell me if you are in fact talking to MySQL 5.7 and not mariadb.   looking at maxscale docs it appears this proxy is compatible with mysql and mariadb equally.  trying to guess that this is mariadb due to seeing "10.x" seems hacky.    we do need to know in a few places that we're either on mariadb or not.

Which means....we might need to just run `@@version` ourselves.   OK.   we'll do that.

* changed **title** from "SQLAlchemy no longer compatible with Mariadb" to "MaxScale proxy server interferes with mysql / mari"

**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

if you can confirm the patch at https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/#/c/zzzeek/sqlalchemy/+/685/ works, that's what we'll be going with

**Curtis McCully ([@cmccully](https://github.com/cmccully)) wrote:**

This patch does indeed work. Thank you so much!

**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

Get MySQL version info from @@version

MySQL dialects now query the server version using ``SELECT @@version``
explicitly to the server to ensure we are getting the correct version
information back.   Proxy servers like MaxScale interfere with the value
that is passed to the DBAPI's connection.server_version value so this
is no longer reliable.

Change-Id: Iafd39be8c9bf1982d58b34cc997ae1016ad6c48c
Fixes: #4205
